# The LAN Shop — Lynnette Hui Xian Ng

> Language, Agents, Networks. The research site of Lynnette Hui Xian Ng
> (ORCID 0000-0002-2740-7818), covering bot detection, coordinated behaviour,
> influence operations and multi-agent social systems.

Lynnette Hui Xian Ng is Deputy Head of the Information Programme Center at DSTA
Singapore and holds a PhD in Societal Computing from Carnegie Mellon University,
where she was advised by Kathleen M. Carley. Her work asks which accounts on a
social platform are automated, what roles they play, how groups of accounts
coordinate, and how such societies can be simulated and governed. She is the
author of 50 publications between 2014 and 2026, listed in full below.

## Tools she built

- **BotBuster** — multi-platform bot detection using a mixture of experts,
  across X, Reddit, Instagram and Telegram.
- **BotSorter** — classifies an account's role rather than bot-or-human:
  amplifier, announcer, repeater, bridge, cyborg, news, content generator,
  self-declared bot.
- **BotBias** — reads a message for the cognitive levers it pulls.
- **Combined Synchronization Index (CSI)** — scores synchrony at user-pair,
  user and whole-network level across hashtags, URLs and mentions, with
  thresholds calibrated from the data rather than fixed by hand.
- **BotSim** — simulates belief contagion in societies of agents.

## Research programmes

- **Design Of The Agents** — what an agent is, how to detect one, and how
  agents and humans influence each other.
- **Simulation** — whether a simulated agent society behaves like a real one,
  and how such simulations can be validated.
- **Networks** — measuring one networked structure against another, and
  telling coordination apart from coincidence.

## Book

*Bots, Bias, and Influence: The Hidden Architects of Social Media*, with
Kathleen M. Carley. Cambridge Scholars Publishing, 2026. ISBN 9781036473112.
https://www.cambridgescholars.com/product/978-1-0364-7310-5
